'''Igor Volodymyrovych Komarov''' ({{Langx|uk|Ігор Володимирович Комаров}}) is a Ukrainian [[Synthetic organic chemistry|synthetic organic chemist]], specializing in [[medicinal chemistry]] and [[nanotechnology]]. He is the director of the Institute of High Technologies of [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://iht.univ.kiev.ua/en/content/igor-komarov|title=Igor Komarov {{!}} Institute of High Technologies|date=2014-06-18|website=iht.univ.kiev.ua|language=en|access-date=2017-08-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810212813/http://iht.univ.kiev.ua/en/content/igor-komarov|archive-date=2017-08-10|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is also a [[Scientific Advisory Panel|scientific advisor]] of Enamine Ltd ([[Ukraine]])<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.enamine.net/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=162|title=Gallery – Enamine|website=www.enamine.net|access-date=2017-08-10}}</ref> and Lumobiotics GmbH ([[Germany]]).

== Career ==
Source:<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://eu.univ.kiev.ua/departments/supramolekulyarnoyi-khimiyi-ka/komarov-igor-volodymyrovych/|title=Biography|last=Komarov|first=Igor|website=Encyclopedia of Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv|access-date=2017-08-10|archive-date=2017-08-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810134336/http://eu.univ.kiev.ua/departments/supramolekulyarnoyi-khimiyi-ka/komarov-igor-volodymyrovych/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Igor V. Komarov graduated [[Latin honors|with distinction]] from Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, and started to work at the same university in 1986 first as an [[engineer]]. He obtained his [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree in 1991 in organic chemistry at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv under supervision of Mikhail Yu. Kornilov; the [[Thesis|candidate thesis]] was devoted to the use of [[lanthanide shift reagent]]s in [[Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy|NMR spectroscopy.]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mydisser.com/en/catalog/view/126705.html|title=Study of onium salts by NMR in the presence of lanthanide shift reagents|last=Komarov|first=Igor|access-date=2017-08-10|archive-date=2017-08-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807154133/https://mydisser.com/en/catalog/view/126705.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Afterwards, he was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[University of Cambridge|University Chemical Laboratory]] in [[Cambridge]] (1996–1997, [[United Kingdom]]) and at the [https://www.catalysis.de/home/ Institut für Organische Katalyseforschung] in [[Rostock]] (2000–2001, Germany). He holds the Supramolecular Chemistry Chair of Institute of High Technologies at Taras Shevchenko National University. Komarov earned his [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree in 2003; the title of his [[thesis]] is "Design and synthesis of model compounds: study of [[Electronic effect|stereoelectronic]], [[steric effects]], [[reactive intermediate]]s, [[Catalysis|catalytic]] [[Enantioselective synthesis|enantioselective]] [[hydrogenation]] and dynamic [[Protecting group|protection of functional groups]]"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://irbis-nbuv.gov.ua/cgi-bin/irbis_nbuv/cgiirbis_64.exe?Z21ID=&I21DBN=EC&P21DBN=EC&S21STN=1&S21REF=10&S21FMT=fullwebr&C21COM=S&S21CNR=20&S21P01=0&S21P02=0&S21P03=A=&S21COLORTERMS=1&S21STR=%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B2%20%D0%86$|title=Catalogs – Vernadski National Academic Library, Ukraine|website=irbis-nbuv.gov.ua|access-date=2017-08-10}}</ref> He is also a scientific advisor for Enamine Ltd.<ref name=":0" /> and Lumobiotics GmbH. Igor V. Komarov was awarded the title of Professor in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.library.univ.kiev.ua/ukr/vystavka/617/617-2.pdf|title=Professors of Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, biographical directory|date=2014|website=Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv}}</ref>

== Contribution to research ==
Source:<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://science.univ.kiev.ua/en/researchgroups/research.php?ELEMENT_ID=2554|title=Igor Komarov|website=science.univ.kiev.ua|language=en|access-date=2017-08-10}}</ref>

[[File:TA Black Red.jpg|thumb|260x260px|1-Aza-2-adamantanone – a model compound. The fragment which mimics the ''cis–trans'' amide isomerization transition state is shown in red]]
[[File:Photobiotic En.jpg|thumb|444x444px|Photocontrollable [[Antibiotics|antibiotic]], an analogue of the natural antibiotic [[gramicidin S]]]]
The areas of scientific interests of Igor V. Komarov are [[medicinal chemistry]] and [[Organic synthesis|synthesis]] of model compounds, which can be used to obtain new knowledge in [[biochemistry]], [[stereochemistry]], [[theoretical chemistry]], [[catalysis]]. Igor has over 125 [[peer review]]ed [[Academic publishing|research papers]], [[h-index]] 31,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7004891576|title=Igor V. Komarov author's profile|date=August 2019|website=Scopus}}</ref> has guided 8 [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD students]] to date. Igor's scientific group puts the main focus on developing of novel synthetic methods and design of theoretically interesting molecules, part of which were created and synthesized in tight collaboration with Prof. Anthony J. Kirby<ref>http://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/person/ajk1</ref> from [[University of Cambridge|the University of Cambridge]] (United Kingdom). One of such collaborative projects was synthesis, study of stereochemistry and [[Chemical property|chemical properties]] of 1-aza-2-adamantanone and its derivatives. A trimethyl-substituted derivative ("the most twisted amide",<ref>{{Cite news|title=The Most Twisted Amide: Structure and Reactions|last1=Kirby|first1=Anthony J.|last2=Komarov|first2=Igor V.|last3=Wothers|first3=Peter D.|last4=Feeder|first4=Neil|date=1998-04-03|pages=785–786|language=en|work=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=37|doi=10.1002/(SICI)1521-3773(19980403)37:6<785::AID-ANIE785>3.0.CO;2-J|issn=1521-3773|issue=6}}</ref> "Kirby's amide"<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Liu|first1=Chengwei|last2=Szostak|first2=Michal|date=2017-05-29|title=Twisted Amides: From Obscurity to Broadly Useful Transition-Metal-Catalyzed Reactions by N−C Amide Bond Activation|journal=Chemistry – A European Journal|language=en|volume=23|issue=30|pages=7157–7173|doi=10.1002/chem.201605012|pmid=27813178|issn=1521-3765}}</ref>) was designed in the Prof. Kirby's laboratory and synthesized by Igor in 1997 during his postdoctoral stay in Cambridge. In 2014, a [[Parent|parent molecule]] was made in Igor's group in collaboration with Prof. Kirby. The compound modelled the transition state of ''cis''-''trans'' isomerization of [[amide]]s and allowed obtaining fundamental [[knowledge]] about the [[Peptide bond|amide bond]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=The Most Reactive Amide As a Transition-State Mimic For cis–trans Interconversion|last1=Komarov|first1=Igor V.|last2=Yanik|first2=Stanislav|last3=Ishchenko|first3=Aleksandr Yu.|last4=Davies|first4=John E.|last5=Goodman|first5=Jonathan M.|last6=Kirby|first6=Anthony J.|date=2015-01-21|pages=926–930|work=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=137|doi=10.1021/ja511460a|issn=0002-7863|issue=2}}</ref>

Igor V. Komarov started his [[research]] in the area of [[synthetic organic chemistry]] at the beginning of 1990th, working on [[phosphorylation]] of [[Aromaticity|aromatic]] [[heterocyclic compound]]s by [[Phosphorus acid|phosphorus(V) acid]] halides.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Phosphorylation of 1,3-Di(N-alkyl)Azoles by Phosphorus(V) Acid Chlorides — a Route to Potential Haptens Derived from Phosphinic Acids|last1=V. Komarov|first1=Igor|last2=Yu. Kornilov|first2=Mikhail|last3=V. Turov|first3=Aleksandr|last4=V. Gorichko|first4=Marian|last5=O. Popov|first5=Vladimir|last6=A. Tolmachev|first6=Andrey|last7=J. Kirby|first7=Anthony|date=1995-11-06|pages=12417–12424|journal=Tetrahedron|volume=51|doi=10.1016/0040-4020(95)00797-C|issue=45}}</ref> At that time, convenient phosphorylation methods were developed, which now find use, for example, for synthesis of [[Materials science|materials]] applicable for [[uranium]] [[Extraction (chemistry)|extraction]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Silica with immobilized phosphinic acid-derivative for uranium extraction|last1=Budnyak|first1=Tetyana M.|last2=Strizhak|first2=Alexander V.|last3=Gładysz-Płaska|first3=Agnieszka|last4=Sternik|first4=Dariusz|last5=Komarov|first5=Igor V.|last6=Kołodyńska|first6=Dorota|last7=Majdan|first7=Marek|last8=Tertykh|first8=Valentin А.|date=2016-08-15|pages=326–340|journal=Journal of Hazardous Materials|volume=314|doi=10.1016/j.jhazmat.2016.04.056|pmid=27177215}}</ref> Later, working in Rostock, Igor V. Komarov changed the direction of his research and got interested in [[Homogeneous catalysis|homogenous]] [[Enantioselective synthesis|asymmetric catalysis]]. The study of catalysis was carried out using model compounds: functionalized [[camphor]]- and [[tartaric acid]]-derived [[Chirality (chemistry)|chiral]] [[ligand]]s were synthesized such as [[Phosphine|monophosphines]],<ref>{{Cite news|title=Highly Enantioselective or Not?—Chiral Monodentate Monophosphorus Ligands in the Asymmetric Hydrogenation|last1=Komarov|first1=Igor V.|last2=Börner|first2=Armin|date=2001-04-01|pages=1197–1200|language=en|work=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=40|doi=10.1002/1521-3773(20010401)40:7<1197::AID-ANIE1197>3.0.CO;2-G|issn=1521-3773|issue=7}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=New chiral monodentate phospholane ligands by highly stereoselective hydrophosphination|last1=Bilenko|first1=Vitaliy|last2=Spannenberg|first2=Anke|last3=Baumann|first3=Wolfgang|last4=Komarov|first4=Igor|last5=Börner|first5=Armin|date=2006-08-28|pages=2082–2087|journal=Tetrahedron: Asymmetry|volume=17|doi=10.1016/j.tetasy.2006.06.047|issue=14}}</ref> [[diphosphines]],<ref name=":03">{{Cite news|title=Chiral Oxo- and Oxy-Functionalized Diphosphane Ligands Derived from Camphor for Rhodium(I)-Catalyzed Enantioselective Hydrogenation|last1=Komarov|first1=Igor V.|last2=Monsees|first2=Axel|last3=Spannenberg|first3=Anke|last4=Baumann|first4=Wolfgang|last5=Schmidt|first5=Ute|last6=Fischer|first6=Christine|last7=Börner|first7=Armin|date=2003-01-01|pages=138–150|language=en|work=European Journal of Organic Chemistry|volume=2003|doi=10.1002/1099-0690(200301)2003:1<138::AID-EJOC138>3.0.CO;2-O|issn=1099-0690|issue=1}}</ref> and then [[Rhodium]](I) [[Coordination complex|complexes]] with them.<ref name=":03"/> The complexes were used for asymmetric [[Hydrogenation|homogenous hydrogenation]] of [[Prochirality|prochiral]] [[Substrate (chemistry)|substrates]], and the obtained results allowed elucidating the effects of oxo- and oxy-[[functional group]]s in ligands on efficiency and [[Functional selectivity|selectivity]] of the catalysts.<ref name=":03"/> These works led to introduction of efficient catalysts to synthetic practice, like catASium,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sigmaaldrich.com/chemistry/chemical-synthesis/technology-spotlights/catasium.html|title=catASium – Essential Elements for Asymmetric Hydrogenations|work=Sigma-Aldrich|access-date=2017-08-11|language=en|archive-date=2017-08-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811183640/http://www.sigmaaldrich.com/chemistry/chemical-synthesis/technology-spotlights/catasium.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> some of them bearing a camphor-derived ligand ROCKYPhos<ref>{{Cite journal|title=A new hydroxydiphosphine as a ligand for Rh(I)-catalyzed enantioselective hydrogenation|last1=Komarov|first1=Igor V.|last2=Monsees|first2=Axel|last3=Kadyrov|first3=Renat|last4=Fischer|first4=Christine|last5=Schmidt|first5=Ute|last6=Börner|first6=Armin|date=2002-08-14|pages=1615–1620|journal=Tetrahedron: Asymmetry|volume=13|doi=10.1016/S0957-4166(02)00372-5|issue=15}}</ref> (named after the cities [[Rostock|ROstock]] and [[Kyiv|KYiv]]).

Although Igor's interest to the synthesis of chiral ligands has not been faded, he changed the general direction of his research once more, and now he works in the area of [[drug design]].<ref name=":1" /> One of the main design principle is restriction of [[Conformation (chemistry)|conformational mobility]] of the [[Drug discovery|drug candidate]] [[molecule]]s.<ref name=":22">{{Cite news|title=Bicyclic Conformationally Restricted Diamines|last1=Grygorenko|first1=Oleksandr O.|last2=Radchenko|first2=Dmytro S.|last3=Volochnyuk|first3=Dmitriy M.|last4=Tolmachev|first4=Andrey A.|last5=Komarov|first5=Igor V.|date=2011-09-14|pages=5506–5568|work=Chemical Reviews|volume=111|doi=10.1021/cr100352k|issn=0009-2665|issue=9}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Trifluoromethyl-substituted cyclopropanes|last1=Grygorenko|first1=Oleksandr O.|last2=Artamonov|first2=Oleksiy S.|last3=Komarov|first3=Igor V.|last4=Mykhailiuk|first4=Pavel K.|date=2011-02-04|pages=803–823|journal=Tetrahedron|volume=67|doi=10.1016/j.tet.2010.11.068|issue=5}}</ref> Prof. Komarov's research group developed many approaches to synthesis of conformationally restricted [[amine]]s and [[amino acid]]s - the [[Building block (chemistry)|building blocks]] for drug design.<ref name=":22"/><ref>{{Cite news|title=Synthesis and Structural Analysis of Angular Monoprotected Diamines Based on Spiro[3.3]heptane Scaffold|last1=Chernykh|first1=Anton V.|last2=Radchenko|first2=Dmytro S.|last3=Grygorenko|first3=Oleksandr O.|last4=Daniliuc|first4=Constantin G.|last5=Volochnyuk|first5=Dmitriy M.|last6=Komarov|first6=Igor V.|date=2015-04-17|pages=3974–3981|work=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|volume=80|doi=10.1021/acs.joc.5b00323|issn=0022-3263|issue=8}}</ref> Numerous conformationally restricted [[Organofluorine chemistry|fluorine]]-containing amino acids were also designed and synthesized, with a purpose of using them as labels to study [[peptide]]s in [[lipid bilayer]]s by [[Solid-state NMR|solid-state NMR spectroscopy]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Trifluoromethyl-substituted α-amino acids as solid-state 19F NMR labels for structural studies of membrane-bound peptides. Fluorine in Pharmaceutical and Medicinal Chemistry: From Biophysical Aspects to Clinical Applications.|last=Kubyshkin|first=Volodymyr|year=2012|pages=91–138}}</ref>

Igor V. Komarov's group made a contribution to design and synthesis of light-controllable biologically active compounds - [[Photoactivated peptide|photocontrollable peptides]] - potential candidates for [[photopharmacology]] drugs. Photopharmacology drugs can be [[Drug administration|administered]] in the inactive, [[non-toxic]] form, and then activated ("switched on") by [[light]] only when and where required to treat localized [[lesion]]s (e.g.in [[Neoplasm|solid tumors]]).<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Velema|first1=Willem A.|last2=Szymanski|first2=Wiktor|last3=Feringa|first3=Ben L.|date=2014-02-12|title=Photopharmacology: Beyond Proof of Principle|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=136|issue=6|pages=2178–2191|doi=10.1021/ja413063e|pmid=24456115|issn=0002-7863|url=https://pure.rug.nl/ws/files/13153399/ja_2013_13063e_photopharma_revised.pdf|hdl=11370/d6714f52-c2c8-4e48-b345-238e98bcc776|s2cid=197196311 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> The activation by light can be done with very high spatiotemporal precision in the lesion site, leaving the rest of the [[patient]] body unaffected.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Controlling Biological Activity with Light: Diarylethene-Containing Cyclic Peptidomimetics|last1=Babii|first1=Oleg|last2=Afonin|first2=Sergii|last3=Berditsch|first3=Marina|last4=Reiβer|first4=Sabine|last5=Mykhailiuk|first5=Pavel K.|last6=Kubyshkin|first6=Vladimir S.|last7=Steinbrecher|first7=Thomas|last8=Ulrich|first8=Anne S.|last9=Komarov|first9=Igor V.|date=2014-03-24|pages=3392–3395|language=en|work=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=53|doi=10.1002/anie.201310019|issn=1521-3773|issue=13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Direct Photocontrol of Peptidomimetics: An Alternative to Oxygen-Dependent Photodynamic Cancer Therapy|last1=Babii|first1=Oleg|last2=Afonin|first2=Sergii|last3=Garmanchuk|first3=Liudmyla V.|last4=Nikulina|first4=Viktoria V.|last5=Nikolaienko|first5=Tetiana V.|last6=Storozhuk|first6=Olha V.|last7=Shelest|first7=Dmytro V.|last8=Dasyukevich|first8=Olga I.|last9=Ostapchenko|first9=Liudmyla I.|date=2016-04-25|pages=5583–5586|language=en|work=Angewandte Chemie|volume=128|doi=10.1002/ange.201600506|issn=1521-3757|issue=18}}</ref> After the treatment, the photopharmacology drugs can be inactivated ("switched off") by light in order to diminish [[Side effect|side effects]] and [[Environmental protection|environmental burden]].<ref name=":3" />

Another research direction in the Igor V. Komarov's scientific group is navigation of [[chemical space]]. A method of structural comparison for organic molecules was developed which employed exit vector plot analysis.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Grygorenko|first1=Oleksandr O.|last2=Babenko|first2=Pavlo|last3=Volochnyuk|first3=Dmitry M.|last4=Raievskyi|first4=Oleksii|last5=Komarov|first5=Igor V.|date=2016-02-09|title=Following Ramachandran: exit vector plots (EVP) as a tool to navigate chemical space covered by 3D bifunctional scaffolds. The case of cycloalkanes|url=http://pubs.rsc.org/-/content/articlehtml/2016/ra/c5ra19958a|journal=RSC Advances|language=en|volume=6|issue=21|pages=17595–17605|doi=10.1039/C5RA19958A|bibcode=2016RSCAd...617595G|issn=2046-2069|url-access=subscription}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> [[Enumeration]] of molecules (exhaustive generation of all theoretically possible structures) was carried out for some classes of organic compounds, for example, for conformationally restricted [[diamine]]s.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Focused enumeration and assessing the structural diversity of scaffold libraries: conformationally restricted bicyclic secondary diamines|last1=Grygorenko|first1=Oleksandr O.|last2=Prytulyak|first2=Roman|last3=Volochnyuk|first3=Dmitriy M.|last4=Kudrya|first4=Volodymyr|last5=Khavryuchenko|first5=Oleksiy V.|last6=Komarov|first6=Igor V.|date=2012-08-01|pages=477–487|language=en|work=Molecular Diversity|volume=16|doi=10.1007/s11030-012-9381-2|issn=1381-1991|issue=3}}</ref>

In the area of [[nanotechnology]], Igor V. Komarov's research group studied [[cell-penetrating peptide]]s as carriers for carbon-based [[Fluorescence|fluorescent]] [[nanoparticle]]s, shuttling them inside [[Eucaryotic cells|eukaryotic cells]] with the purpose of [[Microscopy|bioimaging]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Delivery of SiC-based nanoparticles into live cells driven by cell-penetrating peptides SAP and SAP-E|url=http://pubs.rsc.org/-/content/articlehtml/2015/ra/c4ra10688a|journal=RSC Advances|date=2015-02-17|access-date=2017-08-11|doi=10.1039/C4RA10688A|volume=5|issue=26|language=en|first1=T.|last1=Serdiuk|first2=I.|last2=Bakanovich|first3=V.|last3=Lysenko|first4=S. A.|last4=Alekseev|first5=V. A.|last5=Skryshevsky|first6=S.|last6=Afonin|first7=E.|last7=Berger|first8=A.|last8=Géloën|first9=I. V.|last9=Komarov|pages=20498–20502|archive-date=2017-08-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811223532/http://pubs.rsc.org/-/content/articlehtml/2015/ra/c4ra10688a|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Igor V. Komarov has a Ukrainian patent,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://base.uipv.org/searchINV/search.php?action=viewdetails&IdClaim=232416|title=Спеціалізована БД "Винаходи (корисні моделі) в Україні"|website=base.uipv.org|access-date=2017-08-07}}</ref> 2 international patents,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://worldwide.espacenet.com/publicationDetails/originalDocument?FT=D&date=20161005&DB=&locale=en_EP&CC=EP&NR=2958934B1&KC=B1&ND=4#|title=Espacenet Original document|website=worldwide.espacenet.com|language=en|access-date=2017-08-07}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://worldwide.espacenet.com/publicationDetails/originalDocument?CC=US&NR=2017051017A1&KC=A1&FT=D&ND=3&date=20170223&DB=&locale=en_EP#|title=Espacenet Original document|website=worldwide.espacenet.com|language=en|access-date=2017-08-07}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> is a co-author of [[Textbook|text-books]] on NMR spectroscopy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://iht.univ.kiev.ua/uk/library/books-ivt|title=Книги і методичні посібники викладачів ІВТ {{!}} Інститут високих технологій|date=2012-01-01|website=iht.univ.kiev.ua|language=uk|access-date=2017-08-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807165713/http://iht.univ.kiev.ua/uk/library/books-ivt|archive-date=2017-08-07|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Scientific projects ==
Igor V. Komarov was a coordinator of scientific projects financed by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (three applied projects devoted to design of therapeutic peptides, including photocontrolled [http://science.univ.kiev.ua/research/theme/themefund/ <nowiki>[1]</nowiki>]), Alexander von Humboldt Foundation (Institute Partnershaft and Research Linkage Programs, in collaboration with the [[University of Karlsruhe]] (Karlsruhe, Germany)[http://www.ibg.kit.edu/nmr/english/26.php <nowiki>[2]</nowiki>] and Leibniz Institute of Molecular Pharmacology (Berlin, Germany)[http://www.leibniz-fmp.de/de/research/chemical-biology/res-groups-chembio/dathe-oehlke/projectspeptidelipidinteractio.html <nowiki>[3]</nowiki>]), private companies [[Degussa]] (the project was devoted to development of large-scale production of a ligand for Rhodium-based catalysts of asymmetric hydrogenation) and Enamine (six medicinal chemistry projects, lead discovery and lead optimization). He is currently a coordinator of a European [[Horizon 2020]] Research and Innovation Staff Exchange (RISE) Programme (2016–2019) Grant Agreement number: 690973 [http://pelico.org/ <nowiki>[4]</nowiki>], the title of the project – “Peptidomimetics with Photocontrolled Biological Activity”.

== Awards and grants ==
* [[NATO]] Research Award ([[postdoctoral fellowship]], 01.1996–01.1997, The University of Cambridge, United Kingdom);
* [http://www.uic.unn.ru/new_grant/intas1.htm INTAS] grants (research visits, 08.1993 and 10.1994, The University of Cambridge, United Kingdom);
* [http://www.ifs.se/ ISF grants] (1998, research project, Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv);
